newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Max sees gain from Norseman upgrade.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Max sees gain from Norseman upgrade.

text.p: Max Resources Ltd said on Friday the operator of the Australian Norseman gold project had made a "significant upgrade" in the calculation of the Selene prospect at the south end of the project where Max has a 30 percent interest.

"This resource upgrade has boosted Max's interest in the total project resource by almost 30,000 ounces to approximately 105,000 ounces of gold," the New Zealand-based resource investor said in a statement.

"The operator now considers the total project area is shaping up as a major new gold discovery given the grades, widths, strike-lengths and potentially low stripping ratios which the exploration results to date have outlined.
"The total measured and inferred resource is now in excess of 14.5 million tonnes at 1.65 grams per tonne equating to in excess of 750,000 ounces," Max said.
Max said the operator had begun a bankable feasibility study on the economics of commencing mining operations which is expected to be completed by the end of the year.
